sources.institution: The Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute, Stanford University

evidence.estrutura: Her preference for grassroots local leadership and suspicion of top-down charismatic control strongly support decentralized organization.
evidence.representacao: Participatory democracy and bottom-up leadership were central to her organizing philosophy.
evidence.poder: Civil-rights activism against segregation, intimidation and political repression strongly favors civil liberties over coercive order.
evidence.imigracao: Her coalition politics and racial equality work support pluralist inclusion, though immigration law was not a core issue.
evidence.diplomacia: Foreign policy was not central, but her movement politics generally favored nonviolent organizing over militarism.
evidence.intervencao: No detailed foreign-intervention doctrine is established; anti-domination principles support restraint.
evidence.economia: Her cooperative organizing and anti-poverty work support cooperative/redistributive economics rather than laissez-faire individualism.
evidence.controle: Grassroots cooperative economics suggests collective organization with skepticism of centralized command; moderate planning.
evidence.religiao: Her activism interacted with church-based civil-rights networks but remained civic and participatory rather than theocratic.
evidence.moral: Racial equality, youth empowerment and grassroots democracy strongly support progressive egalitarian values.
